title: Consequence for NS regularity
html:
Remark. Consequence for NS regularity

A valid QOU constrained by \chi(A) = -6 is NS-singular: \mathrm{Obs}_\partial(A) = 0. The boundary observability vanishes. The classical Navier--Stokes equation permits finite-time blowup.

This result stems from the complementary-subgroup argument (item 3). The core topological obstruction e(\xi)|_\Sigma \neq 0 lacks any mathematical channel to suffer cancellation against the operative analytic correction \delta_n|_\Sigma. They strictly populate complementary summands inside H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m).
